title: Simple and compound interest: practice set 2
sourceNote: Original practice questions written for this group. None of them is a CAT previous-year question.
instructions: 10 questions, 20 minutes, CAT marking: +3 right, -1 wrong multiple choice, 0 for a wrong type-in answer.
Type-in answers take a number only: no %, ₹ or units. Use a decimal, not a fraction.

questions.text: What is the simple interest on ₹7,500 at 6% per annum for 4 years?
In how many years will ₹4,800 earn ₹1,440 as simple interest at 7.5% per annum?
What will ₹8,000 amount to in 3 years at 5% per annum, compounded annually?
₹40,000 is invested for 6 months at 8% per annum, compounded quarterly. What is the interest earned (in ₹)?
The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 6% per annum is ₹90. What is the sum?
A sum of money at compound interest, compounded annually, amounts to ₹6,050 in 2 years and to ₹6,655 in 3 years. What is the sum?
A loan of ₹22,000 is repaid in two equal annual instalments at 20% per annum, compounded annually. The first instalment is paid at the end of the first year. What is each instalment (in ₹)?
The simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 12% per annum is ₹3,600. What is the compound interest on the same sum for 2 years at the same rate, compounded annually?
Priya invests ₹50,000 for 1 year at 12% per annum, compounded quarterly. Sneha invests ₹50,000 for 1 year at 12% per annum, compounded half-yearly. How much more interest does Priya earn?
On a certain sum, the compound interest for 2 years, compounded annually, is ₹2,460, and the simple interest for 2 years at the same rate is ₹2,400. What is the sum (in ₹)?
